path: facade org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64::decode(byte[]) (instance method; reached from the trigger via decode(String))
reasons: Reproduced: the variant compiles; Base64Test::testBase64 fails with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException 'Index 123 out of bounds for length 123', thrown at table[c] in the gold, and the stack goes gold < hop4 < hop3 < hop2 < hop1 < Base64.decode(byte[]) < decode(String) < test. The full suite on the variant fails only testBase64, and test.patch is empty. (a) The gold's javadoc promises to decode 'the Base64 characters found in an array of bytes', so other bytes are skipped. It indexes the table with '{' (123), one past DECODE_TABLE's 123 entries, and the UTF-8 e-acute bytes are negative and can never index any table. The gold throws inside itself. The facade and hops 1, 3 and 4 only fail by propagation. Hop 2 sizes the buffer correctly: text.length/4*3+2 is at least floor(3n/4) for n Base64 characters. (b) Each hop's javadoc matches its code: hops 1, 3 and 4 are pure delegations, and hop 2 sizes the buffer and then trims it, as it states. No hop reads text bytes or indexes the table. (c) The three builder-declared hop edits fail the trigger; the reproduced G9 log confirms this. Widening the table cannot help, because negative bytes still overflow and Arrays.copyOf fills with 0, which is the value of 'A'. I tried a table-aware pre-filter at hop 4 that strips bytes outside [0, table.length) with a regex. It passes the trigger, the four ownership tests and the full suite. It is a bypass, not a competing repair: it moves the gold's per-byte skip decision upstream into a pass-through hop whose documentation says nothing about filtering; it leaves the gold's code contradicting its own documented contract for any direct call; it goes against the evidence convention, which puts the bounds test at the lookup (Base64.isBase64, Base64.decode(byte[],int,int)); and it is far from equally small. (d) The names (decodeBase64Text/Octets/Into, fillBase64Octets, decodeBase64Characters) are neutral and equally out of place in all five hosts. The added lines contain no fault vocabulary. The gold's javadoc does not mention the bounds test. The lie (result length computed in advance from input length and pad count, written directly into an exact-length array) is false, because hop 2 over-allocates and copies. The lie concerns result sizing, not the omitted bounds test. (e) The gold is exactly five calls below the facade, in five different existing classes. The hosts are, in order, the five largest public classes other than Base64 (DoubleMetaphone 1105, DigestUtils 582, ColognePhonetic 492, Metaphone 407, QuotedPrintableCodec 387 lines, all under 1500), which C10f section 1 (largest5) allows. The facade body is the original guard plus one call to hop 1, which passes the private static DECODE_TABLE by value (C10i V1). The facade javadoc carries one added procedural sentence. The trigger is an existing test and the only new failure. (f) The convention is pinned outside the gold: Base64.isBase64 tests 'octet >= 0 && octet < DECODE_TABLE.length' before the lookup; Base64.decode(byte[],int,int), used in production by Base64InputStream.read(byte[],int,int), makes the same bound test and documents 'Ignores all non-base64 characters'; DECODE_TABLE's javadoc limits the -1 translation to characters 'within the bounds of the array'; and testIsArrayByteBase64 (Byte.MIN_VALUE, -125, -10, Byte.MAX_VALUE), testNonBase64Test, testIgnoringNonBase64InDecode and testCodec68 pass on the variant. C10i rules: the variant widens no visibility (DECODE_TABLE stays private and is passed as a value), adds no type, uses no reflection, and keeps the facade signature 'public byte[] decode(byte[] pArray)' with its modifiers, its BinaryDecoder override and its thrown types (none) unchanged. No test is edited.
